issues.note: The since-clause needs the past simple: since I last saw him.
The correction keeps the error and contradicts its own note on the present perfect.
Hedged with usually and also; It's two years since is mainly British. Accurate.
The test is garbled: it says past simple, then contrasts has been. Generic charge is wrong.
Past-perfect narrative since (had not seen her since she left) is excluded by until now.
Same defect: the present perfect in the since-clause is wrong.
Same ungrammatical example; right text and right reason.
The correction should be I have lived / have been living here since I was ten.
Until now excludes the common past-perfect use with a later past reference point.
The definition is too narrow; it should allow a later past point as well as now.
The explanation hedges with usually; 'a point before which' misdescribes since.

findings.F1: Sense 1 example uses the present perfect in the since-clause (since I have last seen him); it should be the past simple.
findings.F2: The learner-error correction 'I am living here since I was ten' is itself wrong; it needs the present perfect.
findings.F3: The sense 2 semantic adaptation note gives a garbled tense test (says past simple, then contrasts has been with took).
findings.F4: The time sense is limited to 'until now' and misses the common use with a later past reference point (past perfect main clause).

missed: The present-perfect rule for the main clause is stated three times (sense 1 explanation, sense 1 grammar adaptation note, learner-error note), against one fact, one field.
